svg.aria-label: How to write 是: 9 strokes · 8 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 是
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 是 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 是.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E6%98%AF.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 是. Medians 1–4 draw 日 first: its left vertical, joined top and right sides, inner horizontal, and closing bottom horizontal. Medians 5–9 then draw a wide horizontal, central vertical, short lower-right horizontal, lower-left falling stroke, and long finishing stroke down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all nine medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, the joined top-right corner, and eight intervening lifts; Noto's lower finishing stroke is broader and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
